scenario: After a long-term imprisonment and while awaiting a parole decision, a convicted thief wants to organise a foundation for young victims of crime. I am the president of the agency who decides about the foundation. The founder would donate 125,000 dollars to the foundation. However, he asks that the foundation would be named after himself, helping clear his name. His victim opposes such a foundation and considers it highly upsetting. If I accept the donation that requires the foundation to be named after the thief, crime victims will benefit from the 125,000 dollars. If I do not do this, the money will be lost.
entities: i,the convicted thief who wants to found and name the foundation after himself,the thief's victim who opposes the foundation,the group of young victims of crime who would otherwise have been helped by the foundation's $125,000
outcomes: The 125,000 dollar donation is not used for the foundation
Young victims of crime do not receive support from the 125,000 dollars
The convicted thief does not receive the reputational benefit of the foundation name
The victim is spared the upset of a foundation being named after the thief
